path.title: ABUT: Two places abut if they meet but do not partially coincide. NOTE: OWL 1.1: 'abut' is irreflexive and disjoint with 'partially-coincide'. Symmetric.
CONNECT: Two places are connected if they are both relatively fixed and when they meet.

COVER: Definition cover: cover(a, b) iff forall x:( meet(x, b) implies meet(x, a) ). Specifies that two places cover eachother. Note: this cover-relation is the inverse of the COV relation described by Donnelly (2005). To add in OWL 1.1: 'cover' is reflexive, 'cover' is transitive. LKIF also names the inverse, 'covered by'. Transitive.

EXACTLY_COINCIDE: Definition exactly-coincide: exactly-coincide(a, b) iff forall x:( meet(x, a) iff meet(x, b) ). To add in OWL 1.1: 'exactly-coincide' is reflexive, 'exactly-coincide' is symetric, 'exactly-coincide' is transitive. Symmetric. Transitive.
EXTERNALLY_CONNECT: Two places are externally connected if they are relatively fixed and abut, but do not overlap (OWL 1.1).
IN: The 'in' property is used to express that one place is located (i.e. contained) within another place. It is therefore a mereological relation as well.
MEET: Specifies that two places meet, but need not overlap or cover (reflexive). To add in OWL 1.1: 'meet' is equivalent with ('abut' union 'partially-coincide'). Symmetric.
OVERLAP: Two places overlap if they are relatively fixed and partially coincide.

PARTIALLY_COINCIDE: Definition partially-coincide: partially-coincide(a, b) iff exists x :( cover(a, x) and cover(b, x) ). To add in OWL 1.1: 'partially-coincide' is reflexive, 'partially-coincide' is disjoint with 'abut'. Symmetric.

RELATIVELY_FIXED: NOTE: This cannot currently be expressed using OWL DL. Two places are relatively fixed if and only if either x and y have a common reference object or neither x nor y has a reference object. Symmetric. Transitive.
SPATIAL_RELATION: A spatial relation is a relation between two places.

AUTHOR: Relates an expression to the author of the expression (e.g. for expressions contained in documents).

AFTER: 'after' is the transitive closure of 'next'; this is defined in time-rules.owl. Specifies that a time period occurs after another period, but might overlap with it. LKIF also names the inverse, 'before'. Transitive.
DURING: Specifies that a time period occurs during another period.
FINISHES: Specifies that a time period finishes another period, i.e. the other period starts before, but ends at the same moment.

IMMEDIATELY_AFTER: 'is_met_by' is renamed to 'immediately_after'. Add to OWL 1.1: 'immediately_after' is serial, 'immediately_after' is irreflexive. Specifies that a time period occurs immediately after another period, i.e. it starts where the other period ends. LKIF also names the inverse, 'immediately before'. Every TemporalOccurrence has one or more 'immediately after' that is a TemporalOccurrence. Every TemporalOccurrence has one or more 'immediately before' that is a TemporalOccurrence.
OVERLAP: Specifies that a time period overlaps with another time period (in any way).
PRECEEDS: Specifies that a time period preceeds another period, the periods do not overlap.
STARTS: Specifies that a time period starts another period, i.e. the other period starts at the same time, but ends at a later time.
TEMPORAL_RELATION: A relation between two time periods.

Every PhysicalProcess is also a PhysicalEntity
Every PhysicalProcess is also a Process
Every Place is also a SpatioTemporalOccurrence
Every Plan is also a MentalObject
Every PotestativeExpression is also a LegalExpression
Every PotestativeRight is also a EnablingPower
Every Precedent is also a LegalSource
Every PrivateLegalPerson is also a LegalPerson
Every Problem is also a Observation
Every Process is also a Change
Every Proclamation is also a LegalSource
Every ProfessionalLegalRole is also a SocialLegalRole
Every ProfessionalLegalRole is also a OrganisationRole
Every Prohibition is also a Permission
Every Promise is also a CommunicatedAttitude
Every Proposition is also a MentalObject
Every PropositionalAttitude is also a MentalObject
Every PublicAct is also a Action
Every PublicBody is also a LegalPerson
Every PublicLimitedCompany is also a Company
Every Qualification is also a MentalObject
Every QualificatoryExpression is also a LegalExpression
Every Qualified is also a Thing
Every Reaction is also a Action
Every Reason is also a EpistemicRole
Every Regulation is also a LegalDocument
Every RelativePlace is also a Place
Every Resolution is also a InternationalAgreement
Every Resolution is also a SoftLaw
Every Right is also a Norm
Every Role is also a SubjectiveEntity
Every SocialLegalRole is also a LegalRole
Every SocialLegalRole is also a SocialRole
Every SocialRole is also a Role
Every Society is also a PrivateLegalPerson
Every SoftLaw is also a LegalSource
Every SpatioTemporalOccurrence is also a Occurrence
Every SpeechAct is also a Creation
Every StatementInWriting is also a CommunicatedAttitude
Every Statute is also a LegalDocument
Every StrictlyAllowed is also a Allowed
Every StrictlyDisallowed is also a Disallowed
Every SubjectiveEntity is also a MentalEntity
Every Surprise is also a Observation
Every TemporalOccurrence is also a SpatioTemporalOccurrence
Every Termination is also a Change
Every Trade is also a Transaction
Every Transaction is also a CollaborativePlan
Every Treaty is also a InternationalAgreement
Every Treaty is also a LegalDocument
Every Unincorporated is also a Corporation
Every Whole is also a AbstractEntity

g.title: Thing — Anything at all: owl:Thing, which every LKIF class specialises. The label every node carries, and the end of the relationships LKIF leaves open to any individual, e.g. what a role is played by. Properties: uri
AbsolutePlace — An absolute place is defined without reference to other places. Properties: uri

AbstractEntity — An abstract concept is a concept which does not (necessarily) have a referent in either the physical or the mental world. Abstract entities are (proto)mathematical, formal entities, entities which have a purely formal, logical or mathematical meaning. As all concepts are abstractions, one may argue that a separate abstract world is difficult to see. In common-sense, a circle has more properties and is less abstract than in mathematics. Even mathematicians marvel about the fact their pure abstractions enable us to predict very concrete things. However, we are not directly concerned with these mappings. The most important is that common-sense knows about a (small) number of proto-mathematical concepts, such as collections, sequences and count-numbers (positive integers). We know also about geometric simplifications such as line, circle, square, cube, etc. These common sense notions might even be the real roots of our mathematics. However, these kind of semi-formal abstractions do not play a very central role… Properties: uri
ActOfLaw — Act of law: a public act by a legislative body which creates an expression with legal status; the legal status depends on the jurisdiction of the legislative body. Properties: uri

Action — An action is a change which is brought about by a single agent, playing a role. The agent is the holder of some indended outcome of the action: an action is always intentional. The intention of the agent has usually corresponds with an expectation the intended outcome to be brought about: the agent believes in some expectation. Note that the intention might not correspond with the *actual* outcome of the action. NOTE (OWL 1.1) the action may actually be 'part of' the intention of the agent, that is: intends some (expression:Intention and Self). Properties: uri
ActionPower — An action-power consists in a generic power to produce a legal effect through an action determining it. Also called Subjections. Properties: uri
Agent — An agent is any owl:Thing which can act, i.e. play the 'actor' role wrt. an action. It is a holder for propositional attitudes. Properties: uri
Allowed — See normatively qualified. Alternative labels: permitted, sanctioned, let, licensed. Properties: uri
AllowedAndDisallowed — Something which is both allowed and disallowed through some norm. Properties: uri
Argument — An argument is a reason that is expressed through some medium. Properties: uri
Artifact — A physical object created by some person to fulfill a particular purpose. Properties: uri

Assertion — The assertion is subject to a fit between words and world, in Searle's terms. It's propositional content can be true of false. If it is inconsistent with other assertions, beliefs, observations, it may come to be considered false. Properties: uri
Assignment — A public act that attributes a power to perform a public act to a public body. Properties: uri

Association — A voluntary association (also sometimes called an unincorporated association, or just an association) is a group of individuals who voluntarily enter into an agreement to form a body (or organization) to accomplish a purpose. Equivalent to Society. Properties: uri
Assumption — Proposes something that usually is the case, although there is no specific evidence that it is true in this particular case. Properties: uri
Atom — An atom has no parts. Properties: uri
Belief — Someting an agent 'believes in', i.e. holds as true. Properties: uri
BeliefInViolation — A belief in some violation. Properties: uri
Cause — A cause is an epistemic role played by something which is the outcome of a (chain) of processes. Properties: uri
Change — A change is a difference between the situation before and after the change occurs (the event of the change). A change can be instantaneous. Properties: uri

CoOperative — An autonomous association of persons united voluntarily to meet their common economic, social, and cultural needs and aspirations through a jointly-owned and democratically-controlled enterprise. Properties: uri
Code — A legal code bears one or more norms, all of which are uttered by some legislative body. It cannot bear expressions which are not uttered by a legislative body. Properties: uri

CodeOfConduct — A code outlining the responsibilities of or best practice for an individual or organisation, such as a set of principles of good corporate behaviour adopted by a business. Properties: uri
CollaborativePlan — A collaborative plan is a plan which is shared (and executed) between at least two agents a and b. NOTE: this definition cannot currently be expressed in OWL. Properties: uri
CommunicatedAttitude — A communictated attitude is a propositional attitude involved in an act of communication. Properties: uri

Company — A company refers to a legal entity formed which has a separate legal identity from its members, and is ordinarily incorporated to undertake commercial business. Although some jurisdictions refer to unincorporated entities as companies, in most jurisdictions the term refers only to incorporated entities. Equivalent to the union of LimitedCompany and PublicLimitedCompany. Properties: uri
Composition — A composition has multiple parts, the components should meet. Properties: uri
ComprehensivePlace — A place is comprehensive if it always covers every place (and thus also every location-complex) and every object. NOTE: definition requires OWL 1.1 semantics. Properties: uri
Continuation — The continuation of a change, once initiated. Properties: uri

Contract — A contract bears one or more norms, all of which are uttered by some natural person or legal person. It cannot bear expressions which are uttered by a different kind of agent. Properties: uri

Corporation — A corporation is a legal entity which, while being composed of natural persons, exists completely separately from them. This separation gives the corporation unique powers which other legal entities lack. Equivalent to the union of Unincorporated, Foundation and Incorporated. Properties: uri
Creation — An act which results in the creation of some entity/individual. Properties: uri
Custom — The collective memory of some group of agents, i.e. propositions beared by custom are shared (i.e. held) by all members of the group. Properties: uri
CustomaryLaw — In law, custom, or customary law consists of established patterns of behaviour that can be objectively verified within a particular social setting. Properties: uri

Decision — Decision: A (written) decision of a public body to perform a public act using a public power assigned by law. NOTE: Cannot express that the 'promised' act corresponds to the act qualified by the statement in writing. Properties: uri

Declaration — Searle: the successful performance of a declaration is sufficient to bring about the fit between words and world, to make the propositional content true. In other words, if there is an inconsistency between the declaration and assertions, beliefs, or observations, it is not the declaration that is false. True of definitions and norms, and several other performative statements by legislators. Properties: uri

DeclarativePower — A declarative power covers the case when an effect is produced through the party’s declaration of it. We say that j has the declarative power to realize A to mean that if j declares A, then it is legally valid that A. For example, if x has the declarative power to terminate y’s obligation toward x to do then if x declares that y’s obligation toward x finishes, then it is legally valid that this obligation finishes. Properties: uri
Decree — The word decree is often used as a derogative term for any authoritarian decision. Properties: uri
DefinitionalExpression — A definition in a legal context (for example “x means y” or “by x it is meant y”);. Properties: uri
Delegation — Delegate: entrust a task or responsibility to some other person. Properties: uri
Desire — A feeling of wanting. Properties: uri

Directive — Examples are European Union directive, a legislative act of the European Union and Directives, used by United States Government agencies (particularly the Department of Defense) to convey policies, responsibilities, and procedures. Properties: uri
Disallowed — See Qualified. Alternative labels: violation, prohibited, forbidden. Properties: uri

DisallowedIntention — The propositional content (i.e. that which is intended) of the intention is disallowed. Interesting concept for establishing mens rea (guilty mind), although 'disallowed' is a weaker qualification than criminal. Note the distinction between purposely committing a crime and knowingly committing a crime. The crime committed does not have to match the crime intended for establishing intent! Properties: uri
Document — A Document bears some (and only) expression(s) stated by some statement in writing. Properties: uri
EnablingPower — An enabling power is used in cases where the law aims at enabling some agent to produce an effect in a particular way. Properties: uri
EpistemicRole — The role of something used in a (mental) reasoning/inference process. Properties: uri
EvaluativeAttitude — An evaluative attitude expresses e.g. a judgment. The proposition qualified by the evaluative attitude is comparable to something else. Properties: uri

EvaluativeExpression — A legal evaluative expression asserts that something is good or bad, is a value to be optimised or an evil to be minimised (for example “human dignity is value”, “participation ought to be promoted”);. Properties: uri

EvaluativeProposition — Some thing which is evaluatively qualified, i.e. an evaluation applies to the proposition, the proposition is judged. The proposition is comparable to some other proposition. Properties: uri
Evidence — Observation and/or statement, used as a backing for a belief. Evidence is the role of observation which is qualified by some belief. Properties: uri

Exception — An exception is something that is excluded from a general statement or does not follow a rule. In LKIF rules, an exception is a rule which has an exception relation to another rule (cf. Deliverable 1.1). Properties: uri

ExclusionaryRight — An exclusionary right concerns the prohibition against performing certain inferences (against reasoning in certain ways), or against using certain kinds of premises for certain purposes, in the interest of a particular person. This is especially the case with anti-discrimination rules. Properties: uri
ExistentialExpression — Establishes or terminates the existence of a legal entity (for example “the company ceases to exist”);. Properties: uri

Expectation — An expectation is a predictive belief held on purely logical grounds, i.e. not based on direct external evidence, like an observation or a statement by another agent. It is also often characterized as a "belief about the future", but this isn't very helpful since one may also hold expectations about the (yet unknown) past. The theory of evolution is for instance a fertile ground for predictions about the existence of past species, and therefore at the same a predictor of future observations. Is not only not an observation by itself, but also the thing being expected cannot be an observation in any sense. Properties: uri
Expression — An expression is a proposition beared by some medium, e.g. a document, and is stated by some communicated attitude. Properties: uri
Fact — A fact is a proposition (about something) which is (commonly) agreed upon to hold as true: it has some backing in evidence. Properties: uri

Foundation — A kind of (philanthropic) organization, set up as a legal entity either by individuals or institutions, with the purpose of distributing grants to support causes in line with the goals of the foundation. Properties: uri
Function — The use or purpose of some object as used in some context. Properties: uri
HohfeldianPower — A hohfeldian power covers any action which determines a legal effect. Properties: uri
Immunity — Also called Disabilities. Properties: uri
Incorporated — An organisation formed into a legal corporation. Equivalent to PublicLimitedCompany. Properties: uri
Initiation — The initation of a change. Properties: uri

Intention — Intention is where the agent expects certain consequences of his or her actions and desires those consequences to occur. This concept must be related to qualification and preference in some way. Properties: uri
InternationalAgreement — An agreement entered into by actors in international law, namely states and international organizations. Properties: uri

InternationalArbitration — International Arbitration is the established method today for resolving disputes between parties to international commercial agreements. As with arbitration generally, it is a creature of contract, i.e., the parties' decision to submit any disputes to private adjudication by one or more arbitrators appointed in accordance with rules the parties themselves have agreed to adopt, usually by including a provision for the same in their contract. The practice of international arbitration has developed so as to allow parties from different legal and cultural backgrounds to resolve their disputes, generally without the formalities of their underlying legal systems. Properties: uri
Interval — An interval is a composition of multiple periods of time. Properties: uri

LegalDoctrine — Legal doctrine is a framework, set of rules, procedural steps, or test, often established through precedent in the common law, through which judgments can be determined in a given legal cas. Properties: uri

LegalDocument — A legal document is a document bearing norms or normative statements. By virtue of this definition the norm-as-propositional-attitude is reified as norm-as proposition. In other words, the norm being expressed through the legal source is an expression of the propositional attitude. Subclasses of legal source can be distinguished through the authority of the agent creating the expression (i.e. the agent holding the norm). Properties: uri
LegalExpression — Legal expressions are created by some legal speech act and qualified by a communicated attitude. Properties: uri

LegalPerson — A legal entity is a natural person or a legal construct through which the law allows a group of natural persons to act as if it were a single composite individual for certain purposes. The most common purposes are lawsuits, property ownership, and contracts. Sometimes referred to as corporate personhood or legal personality, this concept allows for easy conduct of business by having ownership, lawsuits, and agreements under the name of the legal entity instead of the several names of the people making up the entity. A legal entity is not necessarily distinct from the natural persons of which it is composed. Most legal entities are simply amalgamations of the persons that make it up for convenience's sake. A legal entity that does have a separate existence from its members is called a company or corporation. This distinction gives the corporation its unique perpetual succession privilege and is usually also the source of the limited liability of corporate members. Some other legal entities also enjoy limited… Properties: uri
LegalRole — A legal role is a role played in a legal context. Legal role players can be both Agents and other 'things'. Properties: uri
LegalSource — A legal source is a source for legal statements, both norms and legal expressions. In a sense it is literally a 'source' of law. Properties: uri
LegalSpeechAct — A legal speech act creates some propositional attitude towards a legal expression. Properties: uri
LegislativeBody — A legislature is a type of (representative) deliberative assembly with the power to adopt laws. Properties: uri

LiabilityRight — A liability right expresses some right to act that brings with it some liability to perform another (compensating) act. For instance, if some k performs the permitted action A, then k will have to perform another action B for the benefit of j. Properties: uri

LibertyRight — When, for the benefit of a person, this person is both permitted to perform and to omit an action – that is, when the action is facultative – we can say that he or she has a liberty right with regard to that action. Properties: uri
Lie — An assertion that is inconsistent with the beliefs of the speaker. It is *intentionally* false. Properties: uri
LimitedCompany — A limited company is a corporation whose liability is limited by law. Equivalent to Unincorporated. Properties: uri

LocationComplex — A location complex is a relatively stable complex of places referred to as one: it is the maximal collection of places with the same reference object. A location complex only overlaps its own parts (OWL 1.1). Properties: uri
Mandate — Mandate: give (someone) authority to act in a certain way. Properties: uri

MandatoryPrecedent — In law, a binding precedent (also mandatory precedent or binding authority) is a precedent which must be followed by all lower courts. It is usually created by the decision of a higher court, such as the House of Lords in the United Kingdom. Binding precedent relies on the legal principle of stare decisis. Properties: uri
Medium — A medium is a bearer of expressions, i.e. externalised propositions. Propositions become expressions once they are externalised through some medium. Properties: uri

MentalEntity — We made the assumption that our views of the mental world have been developed in analogy with physical processes. Mental objects like thoughts are made of elementary parts: concepts. The contents (substance) of these objects are representations. The conceptual content of thoughts are intended by propositional attitudes, like belief, desire, norm etc. Mental objects are processed or stored in containers like a mind which has parts like various memories. Mental processes like thinking, memorizing, imaging, etc. are operations on mental objects. The energy equivalent of mental processing are emotions: the forces that make us focus our mental energies. There is an important difference between the mental world and the physical. Where physical processes occur causally, mental processes are controlled by an intentional stance. The outcome of mental processes can be the intention to act. The intention to act may consist of a structure of primary actions: a plan. The actions can be aimed at bringing about physical… Properties: uri
MentalObject — Metaphor of physical concepts, i.e. the things we mentally manipulate, either in thought or memory. Properties: uri
MentalProcess — A mental, i.e. non-physical, process that has no physical effects. Examples are (human) thought and reasoning. Properties: uri
Moment — A moment is an atomic period of time, i.e. it cannot be divided into other parts. Properties: uri
NaturalObject — A natural object is an object not created by man. Properties: uri

NaturalPerson — A natural person is a human being perceptible through the senses and subject to physical laws, as opposed to an artificial person, i.e., an organization that the law treats for some purposes as if it were a person distinct from its members or owner. Equivalent to Person. Properties: uri
NonBindingInternationalAgreement — Some international agreement that is not binding under international law. Properties: uri

Norm — A norm is a kind of Qualification. A qualification which normatively qualifies some thing (i.e. some normatively qualified): i.e. a qualification which allows or disallows some thing. Properties: uri

NormativelyQualified — Some thing which is qualified (allowed, disallowed) by a norm, i.e. a norm applies to the thing. Taking the principle of deontic choice to mean that the utterer of a normative statement intends to influence choices made by the addressee of the statement, the qualified thing should is comparable to some alternative. Note that Qualified does not partition into Allowed and Disallowed. Firstly, things can be Allowed by one Norm and Disallowed by another one. Secondly, the logical complement of the thing allowed by a permission is qualified (as worse or equal than the thing allowed), but neither allowed nor disallowed. Properties: uri
Obligation — See prohibition. Equivalent to Prohibition. Properties: uri

ObligativeRight — Directed obligative ought-to-do are also called obligative rights. k has the obligative right that j does A iff it is obligatory, toward k, that j does A. An example of obligative right is “it is obligatory, toward Mary, that Tom pays 1,000 euro to John”. Properties: uri
Obliged — Is allowed by an Obligation, i.e. the alternative is strictly_worse according to the Obligation. Alternative labels: directed, commanded. Properties: uri
Observation — An observation is the role played by some proposition believed to be true or false through observation of an agent. Properties: uri
ObservationOfViolation — An observation of a violation, i.e. of something that is Disallowed. Properties: uri

Occurrence — A consequence of our clear separation of ontology from models of situations (occurrences), is well exemplified in the two ways we look at time and space. Things happen against the canvas of space and time. This 3D canvas moving in time (or whatever metaphor) allows us to index instances of objects and processes. Time and space provide positions in time and space for objects. Positions are in general modeled in some mereological framework. However, the objects and processes as classes have time and space properties in a different way. Space occupied by an object is its inherent property of size or extension. This property was for Descartes even the critical one that separated mental (not: abstract) objects from physical ones. Processes occupy (consume) time; they take some duration. This time resource is inversely related to the consumption of energy. This distinction between position and extension is also made in various other ontologies. However, this distinction is easily obscured by the fact that the… Properties: uri
Organisation — An organisation is a group of other organisations or persons which acts 'as one'. An organisation can be both formal (i.e. created by law or decree) or informal. Properties: uri
OrganisationRole — A role which has a meaning in the context of an organisation: i.e. the role defines a 'position' within sthe structure of roles within an organisation. Properties: uri
Pair — A composition of exactly two parts. Properties: uri
PairOfPeriods — A pair of two time periods. Properties: uri
Part — A part is a part_of some whole. Properties: uri

Permission — Permission allows propositions, to which therefore the predication Allowed applies. The thing(s) allowed is/are a subset of the thing(s) qualified by the permission. If S then P(A) means that S is qualified and S and A is allowed. Properties: uri

PermissiveRight — The negation of a directed obligation is a directed permission. However, it counts as a right, namely, a permissive right, only when such negation is aimed at benefitting the author of the permitted action. Properties: uri
Person — A person is an individual agent. Usually associated with 'human being'. Equivalent to NaturalPerson. Properties: uri
PersonRole — A role played by some person (i.e. not an organisation). Properties: uri
PersonalPlan — A personal plan is a plan which is held (and can be executed) by at most one agent. Properties: uri

PersuasivePrecedent — In law, a persuasive precedent or advisory precedent is a precedent that need not be followed under the legal principle of stare decisis, but is nevertheless followed. Sources of persuasive precedent include the obiter dicta in the judgment of a court whose judgment would otherwise be binding, and the judgments of courts in other jurisdictions where the facts and/or legal system are similar to the case at hand. If a superior court adopts a persuasive precedent, it may become binding in the jurisdiction. Properties: uri

PhysicalEntity — The physical world evolves around two main classes: physical objects and processes. In lkif-core, the physical world evolves around two main classes: physical objects and processes. Objects are pieces of matter, while matter is typed by substances. Objects have mass, extension, viz. form and aggregation state (which limits form). Objects are the specification of the notion that matter, and in particular solid objects, is what makes the physical world relatively stable and observable. We define (physical) situations in the first place by the arrangement of physical objects (entities). Properties: uri
PhysicalObject — A physical object is a physical entity consisting of matter, it has a spatio-temporal extension. Properties: uri
PhysicalProcess — Properties: uri
Place — A place is a spatio-temporal-occurrence. Equivalent to the union of AbsolutePlace and RelativePlace. Properties: uri

Plan — A plan is a structure of multiple other plans or actions. These can be both sequential or concurrent. Usually a plan is referred to in the context of the intention to act of some agent, however when executed the plan itself comes into effect. Properties: uri
PotestativeExpression — Attributes a power to some agent (for example “a worker has the power to terminate his work contract”);. Properties: uri

PotestativeRight — A potestative right is an enabling power which is meant to benefit the holder of the power. For example, if some animal y does not belong to anybody, then x has the potestative-right to start x’s ownership of the animal, by capturing y. Properties: uri

Precedent — In law, a precedent or authority is a legal case establishing a principle or rule that a court may need to adopt when deciding subsequent cases with similar issues or facts. The term may also refer to the collective body of case law that a court should consider when interpreting the law. When a precedent establishes an important legal principle, or represents new or changed law on a particular issue, that precedent is often known as a landmark decision. Properties: uri
PrivateLegalPerson — A legal person as defined in private law. Properties: uri

Problem — A problem is an observation that deviates from an Intention. NOTE: This currently cannot be expressed: OWL DL does not support negation of properties. The definition will be further elaborated once OWL 1.1 is supported by development tools. Properties: uri
Process — A process is a 'causal' change: any change which can be explained through some known or understood causal structure. Every process has some Time_Period as duration. Properties: uri
Proclamation — A proclamation (Lat. proclamare, to make public by announcement) is an official declaration. Properties: uri
ProfessionalLegalRole — A professional legal role is a legal profession of some person, examples: lawyer, judge etc. Properties: uri

Prohibition — Prohibition obliges/allows thing(s), to which therefore the predication Obliged applies, and disallows thing(s), to which therefore the predication Disallowed applies. The union of the thing(s) allowed and the thing(s) disallowed is qualified by the prohibition. The things allowed and disallowed by the prohibition are disjoint (and completely partition the space of things qualified). If S then O(A) means that S is qualified, S and A is obliged/allowed, and S and not A is disallowed. If S then F(A) means that S is qualified, S and A is disallowed, and S and not A is obliged/allowed. The difference between Obligation and Prohibition is in which part of the partition of the qualified space is explicitly described by the normative statement. Alternative label: directive. Equivalent to Obligation. Properties: uri
Promise — A promise is a communicated attitude about some future action or state. Properties: uri

Proposition — A (non logical) proposition is a proposition qualified by a propositional attitude. NB: The proposition used here does not correspond to a proposition in proposition logics. NOTE: In previous versions of this ontology, this class was called 'Qualified'. In lieu of the separation between Proposition and Propositional_Attitude, the intended meaning of that class has been moved to 'Evaluative_Proposition'. Properties: uri

PropositionalAttitude — A propositional attitude connects a person (the holder of the attitude) to some proposition, in fact it expresses some qualification over the proposition. Distinguishing a proposition from the propositional content expressed by it is necessary when properties relating to the thing expressed and properties of the expression itself must be distinguished. For LKIF the distinction between Belief, Intention, Qualification, and Observation is relevant. The distinction between belief/expectation, intention, and observation is relevant for i.a. establishing mens rea (guilty mind). The distinction between beliefs (expressing the content of the mind of an agent) and statements (expressing the content of an act of communication by an agent) is classical. Properties: uri
PublicAct — A public act is an act by some Person or Organisation which creates (at least) a communicated attitude (and thereby an expression). Properties: uri
PublicBody — A public body or body created by an act of law to serve a public interest. Properties: uri
PublicLimitedCompany — Similar to the US corporation, offers several advantages over trading as sole trader. Equivalent to Incorporated. Properties: uri
Qualification — A qualification expresses e.g. a judgment. The thing qualified by the qualification is comparable to something else. Properties: uri
QualificatoryExpression — Ascribes a legal role to a person or an object (for example, “x is a citizen”, “x is an intellectual work”, “x is a technical invention”);. Properties: uri
Qualified — Something that is qualified by some qualification. Properties: uri

Reaction — A reaction is an action that is (at least) performed by an agent that has observed some other action (this is an intensional view): Action <-> Reaction. NOTE: question remains whether some observation is also a *requirement* of the reaction. Furthermore, the current definition ensures that the observed action becomes a top:Mental_Object (i.e. it is internalised). Properties: uri
Reason — Teleological counterpart of cause. Properties: uri
Regulation — A regulation bears one or more norms, all of which are uttered by some legislative body. It cannot bear expressions which are not uttered by a legislative body. Properties: uri
RelativePlace — A relative place is defined by some reference to some object/thing. Properties: uri
Resolution — A resolution is a written motion adopted by a deliberative body. The substance of the resolution can be anything that can normally be proposed as a motion. Properties: uri
Right — A right is the legal or moral entitlement to do or refrain from doing something or to obtain or refrain from obtaining an action, thing or recogition in civil society. Properties: uri

Role — A role is a specification of default behavior and accompanying expectations of the thing 'playing' the role. Similar to actors in a theater who play roles, but are not the roles. Example: student. Properties: uri
SocialLegalRole — A social legal role is played by some agent in the context of legal activities. Properties: uri

SocialRole — A social role is played by some agent in the context of social activities. The social role brings with it some expectation of 'default' behavior of the role-filler. Played_by all (action:Agent and (action:actor_in some (action:Action and (plays some expression:Expectation)))). Properties: uri
Society — An organized group of people associated together for religious, benevolent, cultural, scientific, political, patriotic, or other purposes. Equivalent to Association. Properties: uri

SoftLaw — The term "soft law" refers to quasi-legal instruments which do not have any binding force, or whose binding force is somewhat "weaker" than the binding force of traditional law, often referred to as "hard law", in this context. The term "soft law" initially appeared in the area of international law, but more recently it has been transferred to other branches of law. Properties: uri
SpatioTemporalOccurrence — An occurrence in space-time. Properties: uri

SpeechAct — A speech act (or illocutionary act) creates some propositional attitude which qualifies an expression (which by default is mediated through some medium). The actor of the speech act is the utterer of the atitude (NB cannot be expressed in OWL DL). Properties: uri
StatementInWriting — Not to be confused with the actual writing/document itself, which is the medium of the statement. Properties: uri
Statute — A statute bears one or more norms, all of which are uttered by some legal person. It cannot bear expressions which are uttered by a different kind of agent. Properties: uri
StrictlyAllowed — Loose end. Properties: uri
StrictlyDisallowed — Loose end. Properties: uri

SubjectiveEntity — A subjective entity is ontologically subjective, i.e. its existence is relative to an observer, that attributes its properties to some other entity, given a context. Properties: uri

Surprise — A surprise is an observation that deviates from an expectation. NOTE: This currently cannot be expressed: OWL DL does not support negation of properties. The definition will be further elaborated once OWL 1.1 is supported by development tools. Properties: uri
TemporalOccurrence — A period of time, has a duration. Properties: uri
Termination — The termination of a change. Properties: uri

Trade — A trade is an exchange of some things between two agents a and b. Consists of two actions A and B where a is the actor of action A and the recipient of action B, and vice versa. Usually these actions are performed concurrently, but these may also be done consequently. The ownership of the things being traded is the requirement/result pair for each action. Properties: uri

Transaction — A transaction is an exchange or interaction between at least two agents a and b. Consists of two actions A and B where a is the actor of action A and the recipient of action B, and vice versa. Usually these actions are performed concurrently, but these may also be done consequently. Properties: uri

Treaty — A treaty is a binding agreement under international law entered into by actors in international law, namely states and international organizations. Treaties are called by several names: treaties, international agreements, protocols, covenants, conventions, exchanges of letters, exchanges of notes, etc. Properties: uri
Unincorporated — Equivalent to LimitedCompany. Properties: uri
Whole — A whole has at least some part. Properties: uri
